key_moments.title: Intro – ACE Inhibitors vs. ARBs Overview (NCLEX high‑yield)
Members: Grab the Cardio Pharm Guides (make it stick)
Big Concept: These drugs lower BP, not HR (+ “-pril” ACE first‑line)
ARBs (“-sartan”) second‑line — also lower BP, not HR
Nursing Question: Bradycardia less than 60? Do you hold? (Hold for low BP, not low HR)
Mechanism Made Simple: Blocking RAAS → less aldosterone, less sodium/water, more potassium
Side Effects (ACE mnemonic): Avoid pregnancy, Angioedema (ACE only), Cough (ACE only), Elevated K
Potassium Safety Teaching: High‑K foods, salt substitutes, and what to avoid
Hyperkalemia Clues: Muscle spasms, peaked T waves, ST changes — first action is cardiac monitor
The “3 A’s” Recap: Antihypertensive, Avoid pregnancy, Added potassium (hyperkalemia)
First‑Dose Phenomenon: Don’t leave bedside — monitor for big BP drop
Next Steps: NCLEX review series, live CRAM, study guides + practice Qs
